entries.keywords: five senses sight hearing smell taste touch eyes ears nose tongue skin
entries.a: We have five senses: sight (eyes), hearing (ears), smell (nose), taste (tongue) and touch (skin). They help us learn about the world and stay safe.

entries.keywords: living things non living characteristics grow reproduce breathe move
entries.a: Living things move, grow, feed, breathe, sense the world, make young and get rid of waste. Plants, animals and people are living. Stones, water and chairs are non-living.

entries.keywords: animal groups mammals birds reptiles fish amphibians insects classification vertebrates
entries.a: Animal groups: mammals (feed milk to young, like cows and elephants), birds (feathers, lay eggs), reptiles (dry scaly skin, like crocodiles), amphibians (live on land and in water, like frogs), fish (gills, live in water) and insects (6 legs, 3 body parts).

entries.keywords: digestion digestive system stomach intestine mouth food breakdown
entries.a: Digestion breaks food into tiny parts the body can use. Food goes in the mouth (teeth chew), down the oesophagus to the stomach (mixes with acid), then the small intestine (nutrients pass into the blood) and the large intestine (water is absorbed). Waste leaves the body.

entries.keywords: balanced diet nutrients carbohydrates proteins fats vitamins minerals fibre water
entries.a: A balanced diet has: carbohydrates for energy (sadza, rice), proteins for growth (beans, meat, eggs), fats for energy store, vitamins and minerals for health (fruit and vegetables), fibre for digestion and plenty of water.

entries.keywords: teeth brushing dental cavities tooth decay sugar
entries.a: Look after your teeth: brush twice a day, eat less sugar, eat fruit and vegetables and visit a clinic if you have toothache. Sugar and germs cause tooth decay.

entries.keywords: force forces push pull friction gravity balanced newton
entries.a: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can start, stop, speed up or change the direction of a movement. Friction slows things when surfaces rub. Gravity pulls things toward the Earth. Forces are measured in newtons (N).

entries.keywords: magnet magnets magnetic north south poles attract repel iron
entries.a: A magnet attracts iron, steel, nickel and cobalt. It has a north and south pole. Opposite poles attract; the same poles repel. Plastic, wood and paper are not magnetic.

entries.keywords: electricity circuit battery bulb switch conductor insulator current
entries.a: An electric circuit needs a power source (battery), wires and a device (bulb) in a complete loop. A switch opens or closes the loop. Conductors (metals) let electricity flow; insulators (plastic, rubber) do not. Never touch sockets or fallen wires.

entries.keywords: light shadow reflection mirror transparent opaque translucent sun source
entries.a: Light comes from sources like the sun and lamps. It travels in straight lines. A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light. Transparent materials (glass) let light pass; translucent ones let some through. Mirrors reflect light.

entries.keywords: sound vibration pitch loud volume ear hearing travel
entries.a: Sound is made by vibrations. It travels through air, water and solids, but not through empty space. A high pitch comes from fast vibrations; loudness comes from big vibrations. Very loud noise can damage your ears.

entries.keywords: soil types sand clay loam humus erosion fertile
entries.a: There are three main soil types: sandy (drains fast), clayey (holds water, sticky) and loam (a mix, best for crops). Humus from rotting plants makes soil fertile. Soil erosion is the wearing away of soil by wind or water.

entries.keywords: physical change chemical change reversible irreversible burning rusting melting dissolving
entries.a: A physical change can be reversed (melting ice, dissolving salt). A chemical change makes a new substance and usually cannot be reversed (burning wood, rusting iron, baking a cake).

entries.keywords: acid base alkali ph indicator litmus neutral
entries.a: Acids (lemon juice, vinegar) turn blue litmus red and have pH below 7. Alkalis (soap, baking soda) turn red litmus blue and have pH above 7. Pure water is neutral, pH 7. Acid + alkali make salt and water (neutralisation).

entries.keywords: atom atoms proton neutron electron element compound molecule periodic table
entries.a: An atom has a nucleus with protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge), and electrons (negative) around it. An element has one kind of atom (oxygen). A compound joins different elements (water is H2O).

entries.keywords: respiration breathing aerobic glucose oxygen carbon dioxide energy cells
entries.a: Respiration releases energy from food in cells: glucose + oxygen gives carbon dioxide + water + energy. It is different from breathing, which is how air gets in and out of the lungs.

entries.keywords: renewable energy solar wind hydro fossil fuels coal pollution
entries.a: Renewable energy does not run out: solar, wind and hydro (like Kariba). Fossil fuels (coal, oil) will run out and add pollution. Saving electricity and using solar helps the environment.

entries.keywords: habitat ecosystem environment conservation pollution deforestation wildlife
entries.a: A habitat is where a plant or animal lives. An ecosystem is living things and their environment working together. We protect them by planting trees, not littering, saving water and protecting wildlife.

entries.keywords: germs disease prevent cholera typhoid vaccine immunisation clean water washing
entries.a: Germs cause diseases. Prevent them by washing hands with soap, drinking clean or boiled water, using toilets, covering food and getting vaccines from the clinic. Tell an adult and go to the clinic if you feel very sick.
